about: Assembly tree golden vectors. The rules: DIDSA-CAD docs/assembly-tree/spec.md. Generated by DIDSA-CAD tools/assembly_tree_vectors/generate.py from its reference implementation; never edit by hand. `trees` are GET /parts/{id}/assembly-tree responses (ids are made up); `cases` are rows or reveal cases over them.

cases.name: rover_collapsed
cases.why: The default: the root open, everything below collapsed; group rows, folders, bubbles on collapsed rows.

cases.name: rover_both_wheels_open
cases.why: One sub-assembly placed twice: the same child ids get distinct keys under each placement (wheel_l/hub, wheel_r/hub); an open row's bubble is its own mates only.

cases.name: rover_wheel_group_open
cases.why: A group open under one placement only: its key includes the parent's path; members are numbered Bolt M4 <1>..<4>.

cases.name: rover_four_deep_with_features
cases.why: Four levels open down to a part, with its features listed under it (keys <path>#feature:<id>); the missing cable has a generated file name: Component 2.

cases.name: rover_open_part_without_features_yet
cases.why: An open part whose features the client has not fetched: no rows under it yet, still open.

cases.name: rover_screws_group_open
cases.why: The root-level group open: key #group:s1; the renamed screw stays a row of its own where it was.

cases.name: rover_grouping_off
cases.why: Grouping switched off: the repeats are listed one by one with their numbers.

cases.name: rover_folders_open
cases.why: The root's Mates and Patterns folders open (their contents are the client's: not rows here); an open key on a row that cannot open (a missing file) is ignored.

cases.name: rover_unsaved
cases.why: Unsaved is client state: an unsaved Part's rows say unsaved over a lesser state; a worse problem below still wins the bubble.

cases.name: unsaved_bubble
cases.why: A collapsed row counts the unsaved rows below it (one per placement); a suppressed placement adds nothing above but keeps its own bubble.

cases.name: unsaved_open
cases.why: ...open: the rows themselves say unsaved; an unsaved sub-assembly Part marks its own row too.

cases.name: rover_unsaved_root
cases.why: The root's own Part unsaved: the root row says so.

cases.name: rover_no_status
cases.why: Without ?status=true: no constraint states, only missing / cycle / unsaved / fixed flags; bubbles count missing files and cycles only.

cases.name: rover_no_status_grouping_off
cases.why: Without status, grouping off.

cases.name: names
cases.why: Every name fallback: override, Part name, file name, Component N; generated names skipped; numbering per Part (or per file when missing).

cases.name: names_grouping_off
cases.why: Names do not depend on grouping when nothing reaches four.

cases.name: states
cases.why: One row per state slot, and the precedence between them.

cases.name: states_no_status
cases.why: The same rows without status: the fixed flag is the only constraint information left.

cases.name: repeats
cases.why: Missing files group by file; a group sits where its first member was and shows its worst unsuppressed member's state; suppressed members add nothing to its bubble.

cases.name: repeats_open
cases.why: The groups open, and one sub-assembly member open inside its group.

cases.name: repeats_grouping_off
cases.why: Grouping off: four and more are listed one by one.

cases.name: cycle
cases.why: A Part placed inside itself is a cycle row: no children, red, counted on the rows above.

cases.name: cycle_collapsed
cases.why: The cycle counted on the collapsed row above it.

cases.name: deep_capped
cases.why: Stopped at the depth cap: the last node is truncated (no children listed, not expandable when it has no features).

cases.name: wide_capped
cases.why: Stopped at the node cap: only the first nodes are listed.

cases.name: suppressed
cases.why: A suppressed sub-assembly is listed (dimmed) and keeps its own bubble, but adds nothing to the rows above.

cases.name: suppressed_open
cases.why: ...open, its rows show their own states.

cases.name: single_part
cases.why: A Part opened on its own: the root row and its features.

cases.name: reveal_four_deep
cases.why: Reveal a row four levels down: open each ancestor.

cases.name: reveal_top_level
cases.why: A top-level row needs nothing opened.

cases.name: reveal_in_group
cases.why: A row inside a group: open its ancestors and the group.

cases.name: reveal_in_group_off
cases.why: ...with grouping off, only the ancestors.

cases.name: reveal_root_group
cases.why: A top-level member of a group: just the group.

cases.name: reveal_inside_group_member
cases.why: Below a member of a group: the group and the member.
